exercises.name: Finger Flexion
exercises.description: Gently curl the fingers toward the palm to maintain finger joint flexion range.
exercises.starting_position: Rest the forearm on a table with the palm facing up and fingers relaxed.
exercises.required_movement: Slowly bend the fingers into a gentle fist, holding the thumb outside the palm, then slowly straighten.
contraindications: Do not force movement into sharp pain
Avoid if recent finger fracture without clinician clearance

exercises.name: Finger Extension
exercises.description: Open the fingers fully to maintain finger extension range and balance flexor stiffness.
exercises.starting_position: Hand relaxed on a flat surface, palm down.
exercises.required_movement: Lift and straighten the fingers away from the palm, spreading them gently, then relax back.
contraindications: Avoid if extension triggers joint locking or sharp pain

exercises.name: Finger Spreading (Abduction)
exercises.description: Spread the fingers apart to strengthen the intrinsic muscles of the hand.
exercises.starting_position: Palm flat on a table with fingers together.
exercises.required_movement: Spread the fingers as far apart as is comfortable, hold briefly, then bring them back together.
contraindications: Avoid forced spreading if it causes pain in the hand web-spaces

exercises.name: Finger Walking
exercises.description: Walk the fingers forward along a surface to improve coordination and full-range motion.
exercises.starting_position: Palm flat on a table.
exercises.required_movement: Lift and place one finger at a time to 'walk' the hand forward, then reverse back.
contraindications: Avoid if painful in the knuckle joints

exercises.name: Fist Opening and Closing
exercises.description: Open and close the hand into a full fist to maintain composite grip range.
exercises.starting_position: Forearm supported, hand relaxed.
exercises.required_movement: Make a gentle full fist with the thumb wrapped outside the fingers, then open the hand fully.
contraindications: Do not make a tight fist during early healing or acute pain
Avoid with suspected fracture

exercises.name: Thumb Opposition
exercises.description: Touch the thumb to each fingertip to maintain the critical pinch range of the thumb.
exercises.starting_position: Palm facing up, thumb relaxed and adducted.
exercises.required_movement: Touch the thumb tip to the tip of each finger in sequence (index to little finger), then reverse.
contraindications: Avoid if thumb base joint is acutely painful or swollen

exercises.name: Thumb Flexion
exercises.description: Bend the thumb across the palm to maintain thumb flexion mobility.
exercises.starting_position: Hand relaxed, palm facing up.
exercises.required_movement: Slowly bend the thumb across the palm toward the base of the little finger, then return.
contraindications: Avoid forceful movement at the thumb base (CMC) joint

exercises.name: Thumb Extension
exercises.description: Move the thumb away from the palm to maintain thumb extension and abduction range.
exercises.starting_position: Hand resting flat on a table.
exercises.required_movement: Move the thumb out and away from the palm to the side, hold briefly, then return.
contraindications: Avoid if pain radiates along the thumb side of the wrist

exercises.name: Wrist Flexion
exercises.description: Bend the wrist forward and backward to maintain wrist flexion range.
exercises.starting_position: Forearm supported on a table, hand hanging off the edge, palm facing down.
exercises.required_movement: Bend the hand up and then down at the wrist within a pain-free range, keeping fingers relaxed.
contraindications: Avoid end-range stretching if recently injured
Not for weight-bearing during healing

exercises.name: Wrist Extension
exercises.description: Extend the wrist to maintain extension range and stretch the wrist flexors.
exercises.starting_position: Forearm supported, palm facing down, hand hanging off the table edge.
exercises.required_movement: Lift the back of the hand upward as far as is comfortable, then return slowly.
contraindications: Avoid if it reproduces sharp pain on the back of the wrist

exercises.name: Wrist Rotation
exercises.description: Circle the wrist to maintain rotational mobility of the joint.
exercises.starting_position: Elbow supported and bent to 90 degrees, hand relaxed with fingers loosely curled.
exercises.required_movement: Slowly circle the hand in each direction, keeping the forearm still.
contraindications: Avoid fast circular motion in acute inflammation

exercises.name: Wrist Ulnar & Radial Deviation
exercises.description: Move the wrist side to side to maintain full deviation range.
exercises.starting_position: Forearm supported on a table, hand resting flat on its side (thumb up).
exercises.required_movement: Move the hand up (toward the thumb) and down (toward the little finger) in a pain-free arc.
contraindications: Avoid painful end-range at the ulnar styloid

exercises.name: Gentle Grip / Release
exercises.description: Squeeze and release a soft ball to re-train grip strength with low load.
exercises.starting_position: Sitting comfortably, holding a soft therapy ball or rolled sock in the hand.
exercises.required_movement: Gently squeeze the ball, hold for a few seconds, then fully release and straighten the fingers.
contraindications: Not to be performed if a fracture is suspected or in acute pain
Do not use if grip causes joint pain

exercises.name: Towel Wringing
exercises.description: Twist a rolled towel with both hands to strengthen wrist and forearm muscles.
exercises.starting_position: Holding a rolled towel horizontally with both hands, elbows relaxed.
exercises.required_movement: Twist the towel in opposite directions with each hand, then reverse.
contraindications: Not for acute injuries or suspected fracture
Skip if it reproduces wrist pain

exercises.name: Thumb Abduction
exercises.description: Lift the thumb straight away from the palm to open the web-space and maintain thumb range.
exercises.starting_position: Hand flat on a table, palm facing up, fingers relaxed and together.
exercises.required_movement: Move the thumb out and away from the index finger in one plane, hold briefly, then return it gently alongside the hand.
contraindications: Avoid if the thumb base (CMC) joint is acutely painful or swollen
Do not force the thumb backwards

exercises.name: Wrist Ulnar Deviation
exercises.description: Bend the wrist sideways toward the little finger to keep the ulnar deviation range.
exercises.starting_position: Forearm supported on a table, hand resting on its side with the thumb pointing up.
exercises.required_movement: Tip the hand downward toward the little-finger side within a pain-free arc, then return upright.
contraindications: Avoid painful end-range near the ulnar styloid
Stop if clicking with pain occurs

exercises.name: Wrist Radial Deviation
exercises.description: Bend the wrist sideways toward the thumb to keep the radial deviation range.
exercises.starting_position: Forearm supported on a table, hand resting on its side with the thumb pointing up.
exercises.required_movement: Tip the hand upward toward the thumb side within a comfortable arc, then return to the middle.
contraindications: Avoid if pain radiates along the thumb side of the wrist
Keep the motion small and controlled

exercises.name: Individual Finger Flexion
exercises.description: Bend each finger separately into the palm to restore isolated joint control after injury or surgery.
exercises.starting_position: Forearm supported, palm facing up, fingers fully relaxed.
exercises.required_movement: Bend one finger at a time down into the palm (thumb, index, middle, ring, little), hold a moment, then straighten it before moving to the next.
contraindications: Do not force a stiff joint into sharp pain
Avoid after recent tendon repair without clinician clearance

exercises.name: Tendon Gliding Exercises
exercises.description: Move through the fist positions (straight, hook, table-top, full fist) so the finger tendons glide smoothly.
exercises.starting_position: Wrist neutral, forearm supported, palm facing you.
exercises.required_movement: Walk slowly through the positions: straight hand, hook fist, table-top (fingers at 90 degrees), full fist — then reverse back to straight.
contraindications: Not during acute tendon repair without surgeon approval
Reduce range if catching or locking occurs

exercises.name: Forearm Pronation
exercises.description: Rotate the forearm to turn the palm downward, maintaining pronation range for daily tasks.
exercises.starting_position: Elbow bent at 90 degrees and tucked against your side, thumb pointing up.
exercises.required_movement: Slowly rotate the forearm so the palm faces the floor, hold briefly, then rotate back to thumb-up.
contraindications: Avoid if rotation reproduces pain near the elbow or wrist
Keep the elbow still — do not swing the arm

exercises.name: Forearm Supination
exercises.description: Rotate the forearm to turn the palm upward, maintaining supination range for daily tasks.
exercises.starting_position: Elbow bent at 90 degrees and tucked against your side, palm facing the floor.
exercises.required_movement: Slowly rotate the forearm so the palm faces the ceiling, hold briefly, then rotate back down.
contraindications: Avoid end-range forcing after distal radius injuries
Keep the elbow still — do not shrug the shoulder

exercises.name: Elbow Flexion / Extension
exercises.description: Bend and straighten the elbow fully to restore the arm's reaching range after immobilisation.
exercises.starting_position: Sitting tall with the arm at your side, elbow straight, palm facing forward.
exercises.required_movement: Bend the elbow, bringing the hand up toward the shoulder, hold briefly, then lower it back until the elbow is straight.
contraindications: Do not force past the point of sharp pain
Avoid heavy resistance after fracture clearance only allows motion

exercises.name: Finger Adduction
exercises.description: Bring the fingers back together from a spread position to train the intrinsic adductor muscles.
exercises.starting_position: Palm flat on a table with the fingers spread apart.
exercises.required_movement: Slowly bring the fingers together against the surface, then let them fall open again.
contraindications: Stop if the web-spaces pinch painfully

exercises.name: Finger Gliding
exercises.description: Smooth opening and closing cycles that glide the finger tendons through their full sheath.
exercises.starting_position: Forearm supported, palm facing up, fingers relaxed.
exercises.required_movement: Glide the fingers slowly from fully straight to a comfortable fist and back without stopping.
contraindications: Reduce range if tendons catch or snap
Not during acute tendon repair without surgeon approval

exercises.name: Hook Fist
exercises.description: Bend only the finger middle joints to glide flexor tendons while keeping knuckles straight.
exercises.starting_position: Hand flat, palm up, fingers straight.
exercises.required_movement: Bend the fingertips into a hook shape keeping the knuckle joints straight, then straighten again.
contraindications: Avoid forcing if the middle joints are acutely swollen

exercises.name: Straight Fist (Table Top)
exercises.description: Bend at the knuckles with straight fingers to isolate the intrinsic muscle glide.
exercises.starting_position: Hand resting on a table, fingers straight together.
exercises.required_movement: Bend the fingers at the large knuckles keeping them straight, forming a table-top, then return flat.
contraindications: Skip if the knuckles are painful today

exercises.name: Claw Fist
exercises.description: Combine bent knuckles with curled tips to move all finger joints through a claw-and-open cycle.
exercises.starting_position: Elbow supported, hand in front of you, fingers straight.
exercises.required_movement: Curl the fingers into a claw shape with knuckles bent, hold briefly, then open the hand wide.
contraindications: Never force into sharp joint pain
Avoid with recent finger fractures

exercises.name: Finger Tapping
exercises.description: Tap each fingertip against the thumb to build coordination and opposition speed.
exercises.starting_position: Elbows supported, palms facing each other or up.
exercises.required_movement: Tap the thumb to index, middle, ring and little fingertip in turn, keeping movements light and quick but controlled.
contraindications: Slow down if precision is poor — accuracy before speed

exercises.name: Thumb Circles
exercises.description: Circle the thumb gently to mobilise the base joint through its combined arc.
exercises.starting_position: Hand relaxed, palm up, fingers loosely curled.
exercises.required_movement: Draw slow, comfortable circles with the tip of the thumb, first one direction then the other.
contraindications: Avoid if the thumb base is acutely inflamed

exercises.name: Thumb Adduction
exercises.description: Return the thumb alongside the index finger to restore the adducted rest position.
exercises.starting_position: Palm up with the thumb held away from the hand.
exercises.required_movement: Bring the thumb gently alongside the side of the index finger, hold, then lift it away again.
contraindications: Do not force the thumb across the palm if it catches

exercises.name: Thumb Stretch
exercises.description: A gentle sustained stretch across the thumb web-space to reduce stiffness.
exercises.starting_position: Hand flat, palm up, fingers relaxed.
exercises.required_movement: Move the thumb out to the side to a mild stretch and hold for a few seconds before easing back.
contraindications: Stretch must stay mild — never bounce the thumb

exercises.name: Thumb Mobility Flow
exercises.description: Combine abduction, opposition and circles into one flowing thumb mobility sequence.
exercises.starting_position: Hand supported, palm up, wrist neutral.
exercises.required_movement: Flow smoothly: lift the thumb away, circle it, touch it to the little-finger base and return — one continuous cycle.
contraindications: Keep every part of the flow pain-free

exercises.name: Thumb Strengthening (Pinch Cycles)
exercises.description: Repeated gentle pinch presses to strengthen the thumb muscles after injury or splinting.
exercises.starting_position: Elbow supported, hand relaxed.
exercises.required_movement: Press the thumb tip against each fingertip with gentle firm effort, release fully between presses.
contraindications: Only light effort until cleared after thumb fracture or ligament injury

exercises.name: Soft Ball Squeeze
exercises.description: Squeeze a soft ball to gently load the gripping muscles of the hand and palm.
exercises.starting_position: Hold a soft ball or stress ball in the palm.
exercises.required_movement: Squeeze the ball gently, hold for about three seconds, then relax the grip completely.
contraindications: Not during acute pain or suspected fracture
Skip if squeezing causes joint pain

exercises.name: Grip and Release
exercises.description: Alternate quick-but-controlled gripping with full finger opening to train grip switching.
exercises.starting_position: Forearm supported, hand free at the edge of a table.
exercises.required_movement: Close the hand into a comfortable fist, then open it fully and spread the fingers — repeat smoothly.
contraindications: Avoid tight fists early after injury
Reduce speed if cramping starts

exercises.name: Tip Pinch
exercises.description: Precision tip-to-tip pinches that strengthen the small intrinsic pinch muscles.
exercises.starting_position: Elbow supported, thumb and index tip touching.
exercises.required_movement: Pinch the thumb and index tips together firmly but pain-free, release halfway, and repeat.
contraindications: Light effort only after thumb ligament injuries

exercises.name: Three-Finger Pinch
exercises.description: A chuck pinch using thumb, index and middle fingers for functional grasp strength.
exercises.starting_position: Elbow supported; thumb, index and middle fingertips touching.
exercises.required_movement: Squeeze the three pads together, hold two seconds, then open the fingers fully apart.
contraindications: Stop if the finger joints grind with pain

exercises.name: Lateral Pinch (Key Grip)
exercises.description: Press the thumb against the side of the index finger — the key-grip used for turning keys.
exercises.starting_position: Hand on its side, thumb resting against the index finger's outer edge.
exercises.required_movement: Squeeze the thumb sideways against the index finger, hold, then relax without letting the thumb collapse across the palm.
contraindications: Avoid hard squeezing with a healing thumb-base fracture

exercises.name: Palm Press
exercises.description: Press the palm flat and lift the fingers to stretch the palm fascia and activate extensors.
exercises.starting_position: Elbow bent, palms pressed together at chest height.
exercises.required_movement: Press the palms firmly together, then push the fingers away from each other to stretch the palm, and relax.
contraindications: Mild stretch only for Dupuytren's-related tightness

exercises.name: Putty Grip
exercises.description: Squeeze therapy putty through the full hand to build graded grip strength.
exercises.starting_position: Hold a ball of therapy putty in the palm.
exercises.required_movement: Squeeze the putty into the palm slowly, hold, then work the fingers back open through the putty.
contraindications: Use clinician-assigned putty resistance only

exercises.name: Finger Resistance Exercise
exercises.description: Open the fingers against an elastic band to strengthen the spreading muscles.
exercises.starting_position: An elastic band looped around the outside of all five fingertips.
exercises.required_movement: Spread the fingers outward against the band, hold briefly, then close slowly under control.
contraindications: Skip if any finger joint is acutely painful
Use a very light band first

exercises.name: Wrist Circumduction
exercises.description: Circle the hand through its full pain-free arc to mobilise the wrist in every direction.
exercises.starting_position: Forearm supported on a table with the hand free over the edge.
exercises.required_movement: Move the hand slowly in large comfortable circles — up, to the side, down, back — then reverse the direction.
contraindications: Avoid fast circles during acute inflammation
Keep circles small if end-range is painful

exercises.name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
exercises.description: A sustained stretch for the underside of the forearm to lengthen the wrist flexor muscles.
exercises.starting_position: Arm straight in front, palm facing up.
exercises.required_movement: With the other hand, gently pull the fingers and palm back until a mild stretch is felt under the forearm — hold and breathe.
contraindications: Stretch must stay mild after distal radius injury
Never stretch into tingling or numbness

exercises.name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
exercises.description: A sustained stretch along the back of the forearm for tennis-elbow and wrist stiffness.
exercises.starting_position: Arm straight in front, palm facing down, wrist relaxed.
exercises.required_movement: Bend the wrist so the palm faces you, deepening gently with the other hand until the top of the forearm stretches — hold.
contraindications: Ease off if it reproduces lateral elbow pain sharply

exercises.name: Wrist Mobility Flow
exercises.description: Combine flexion, extension and deviations into one smooth wrist mobility sequence.
exercises.starting_position: Forearm supported, hand relaxed at the edge of a table.
exercises.required_movement: Flow through the positions: bend down, sweep up, tip toward the thumb side, tip toward the little side — continuously and smoothly.
contraindications: Stay within the arc that is completely pain-free

exercises.name: Wrist Strengthening (Light Load)
exercises.description: Controlled wrist curls against a very light weight or water bottle to strengthen the wrist movers.
exercises.starting_position: Forearm supported on a table, holding a very light object with the hand free over the edge.
exercises.required_movement: Slowly bend the wrist up and lower it back down through the available range, keeping the forearm still.
contraindications: Only after fracture clearance
Use 0.25–1 kg maximum unless your clinician advises more

exercises.name: Wrist Curl
exercises.description: Palm-up wrist curls loading the forearm flexors through their full range.
exercises.starting_position: Seated, forearm resting on the thigh or bench, palm up, light weight in hand.
exercises.required_movement: Curl the hand upward by bending the wrist, pause briefly at the top, lower slowly.
contraindications: Not during acute medial elbow pain
Light load only until cleared

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl
exercises.description: Palm-down wrist extensions loading the forearm extensor muscles.
exercises.starting_position: Seated, forearm supported, palm facing down, very light weight in hand.
exercises.required_movement: Lift the back of the hand upward by extending the wrist, pause, then lower with control.
contraindications: Reduce load if outer-elbow (tennis elbow) pain flares

exercises.name: Forearm Stretch
exercises.description: Elbow-straightened forearm stretching held statically to restore muscle length.
exercises.starting_position: Standing tall, arm straight out, palm up.
exercises.required_movement: Keep the elbow straight and gently draw the fingers back with the opposite hand until the whole forearm lengthens — hold and breathe.
contraindications: Mild tension only — no pulling into pain

exercises.name: Grip Rotation
exercises.description: Rotate a light held object from upright to horizontal and back to train rotational strength of the forearm.
exercises.starting_position: Elbow bent 90° and tucked to your side, holding a hammer or light object upright.
exercises.required_movement: Rotate the object slowly toward the little-finger side, then back upright and slightly past — like turning a key both ways.
contraindications: Not after recent distal radius fracture without clearance
Keep the elbow still throughout

exercises.name: Elbow Flexion
exercises.description: Bend the elbow fully to restore flexion range for feeding, grooming and reaching tasks.
exercises.starting_position: Sitting or standing tall with the arms at the sides, elbows straight, palms forward.
exercises.required_movement: Bend one elbow bringing the hand toward the shoulder as far as comfortable, then straighten fully back down.
contraindications: Do not force past sharp pain
Only gentle motion after fracture until clinician clearance

exercises.name: Elbow Extension
exercises.description: Straighten the elbow fully to recover extension range lost after splinting or swelling.
exercises.starting_position: Sitting with the elbow bent comfortably, upper arm supported.
exercises.required_movement: Straighten the elbow slowly until fully extended or to the first point of resistance, then bend back with control.
contraindications: Stop at sharp pain — never bounce into extension

exercises.name: Assisted Elbow Flexion
exercises.description: The other hand assists the stiff elbow through its range when active motion alone falls short.
exercises.starting_position: Sitting; grip the forearm just below the wrist with the well hand.
exercises.required_movement: Bend the elbow actively while the other hand gently assists the movement deeper, then assist back down slowly.
contraindications: Assist force stays gentle — this must never be forced
Skip during acute post-operative phase unless prescribed

exercises.name: Controlled Elbow Bending
exercises.description: Slow-tempo elbow bends that build motor control and confidence through the middle range.
exercises.starting_position: Standing tall, arms relaxed at the sides.
exercises.required_movement: Bend and straighten the elbow to a slow three-count rhythm each way, keeping the shoulder relaxed.
contraindications: If trembling starts, rest before continuing

exercises.name: Elbow Extension Stretch
exercises.description: A held straight-arm stretch targeting the elbow's end-range extension stiffness.
exercises.starting_position: Arm out in front or resting on a table, elbow as straight as comfortable.
exercises.required_movement: Prop the wrist on a rolled towel or press gently downward to feel a mild stretch at the front of the elbow — hold and breathe.
contraindications: Mild stretch only after immobilisation
Stop if numbness or tingling appears

exercises.name: Biceps Stretch
exercises.description: A doorway stretch that lengthens the biceps and front-shoulder tissues together.
exercises.starting_position: Stand in a doorway, forearm along the frame with the elbow roughly at shoulder height.
exercises.required_movement: Step forward gently until the biceps and chest front stretch mildly — hold, breathing steadily.
contraindications: Avoid entirely with an acute shoulder dislocation history until cleared

exercises.name: Triceps Stretch
exercises.description: An overhead stretch lengthening the triceps and back of the shoulder.
exercises.starting_position: Sitting or standing tall; raise the affected arm overhead.
exercises.required_movement: Bend the elbow so the hand drops behind the head/neck; assist gently with the other hand until the triceps stretches — hold.
contraindications: Skip with acute shoulder impingement pain overhead

exercises.name: Elbow Pronation / Supination
exercises.description: Turn the palm down and up with the elbow tucked to restore rotational elbow range.
exercises.starting_position: Elbow bent 90° and held against the side, thumb pointing up.
exercises.required_movement: Rotate the forearm until the palm faces the floor, hold briefly, rotate back through neutral until the palm faces the ceiling.
contraindications: Keep the elbow still — no swinging
Gentle range after distal biceps or radial-head injury until cleared

exercises.name: Elbow Mobility Routine
exercises.description: A flowing sequence combining bending, straightening and forearm turns for overall elbow mobility.
exercises.starting_position: Standing comfortably, arms at the sides.
exercises.required_movement: Flow smoothly: bend the elbow fully, straighten it, turn the palm up, turn it down — one continuous cycle per rep.
contraindications: Every part of the flow must remain pain-free

exercises.name: Light Elbow Strengthening
exercises.description: Slow elbow curls against a very light load to rebuild strength safely after deconditioning.
exercises.starting_position: Sitting, holding a very light object (0.5–1 kg) in the hand, arm at the side.
exercises.required_movement: Curl the object up by bending the elbow, pause, then lower over three slow counts.
contraindications: Only after fracture/tendon clearance
Stop immediately with sharp joint pain

exercises.name: Shoulder Flexion
exercises.description: Raise the arm forward and up to restore the shoulder's overhead reaching range.
exercises.starting_position: Standing tall with the arms relaxed at the sides, palms facing the thighs.
exercises.required_movement: Raise one arm straight forward and up as far as comfortable, then lower it slowly along the same path.
contraindications: Stop below painful arcs if impingement pain is present
Avoid heavy speed — smooth only

exercises.name: Shoulder Extension
exercises.description: Take the arm gently behind the body to open the front-shoulder tissues.
exercises.starting_position: Standing tall, arms at the sides, palms facing back.
exercises.required_movement: Keeping the elbow straight, take the arm slowly backward as far as comfortable, then return it alongside.
contraindications: Mild range after dislocation until cleared
Never force into sharp pain behind

exercises.name: Shoulder Abduction
exercises.description: Lift the arm out to the side in the scapular plane to build abduction range.
exercises.starting_position: Standing tall, arms relaxed at the sides, thumbs turned slightly up.
exercises.required_movement: Raise one arm out to the side toward ear height within a pain-free arc, thumb leading, then lower with control.
contraindications: Stay below the painful arc if impingement is present
Do not shrug the shoulder as you lift

exercises.name: Shoulder Adduction (Cross Body)
exercises.description: Draw the arm across the chest to train adduction range and stretch the outer shoulder.
exercises.starting_position: Standing or sitting tall, arm raised to about shoulder height.
exercises.required_movement: Sweep the arm across your chest toward the opposite shoulder, keeping it level, then return it out to the start.
contraindications: Skip during acute rotator-cuff pain
Keep the sweep below the painful arc

exercises.name: Shoulder Internal Rotation
exercises.description: Reach behind toward the lower back to maintain internal rotation range.
exercises.starting_position: Standing; rest the hand by your hip.
exercises.required_movement: Bend the elbow and reach the back of the hand gently toward the small of your back, then return the arm down.
contraindications: Never force behind-the-back reach after dislocation until cleared

exercises.name: Shoulder External Rotation
exercises.description: With the elbow pinned at your side, rotate the forearm outward like opening a door.
exercises.starting_position: Elbow bent 90° and tucked against your ribs, palm facing inward.
exercises.required_movement: Rotate the forearm outward away from the body keeping the elbow still, pause, and bring it slowly back.
contraindications: Small range after subluxation/dislocation until surgeon clearance

exercises.name: Shoulder Circumduction
exercises.description: Large gentle circles of the whole arm to mobilise the shoulder through its combined arc.
exercises.starting_position: Standing tall with the arm hanging relaxed or held lightly forward.
exercises.required_movement: Swing the arm in large, slow, comfortable circles forward several times, then reverse direction.
contraindications: Reduce circle size if any arc pinches painfully

exercises.name: Cross-Body Shoulder Stretch
exercises.description: A held stretch pulling the arm across the chest to release the posterior shoulder.
exercises.starting_position: Standing tall; raise one arm to chest height across the body.
exercises.required_movement: Hook the other hand above the elbow and draw the arm gently closer to the chest until the back of the shoulder stretches — hold.
contraindications: Mild pull only — never yank the elbow across

exercises.name: Doorway Shoulder Stretch
exercises.description: A frame-supported hold that opens the chest and front-shoulder muscles.
exercises.starting_position: Forearms on a door frame with elbows just below shoulder height.
exercises.required_movement: Lean gently through the doorway until the chest and front shoulders stretch mildly — hold and breathe steadily.
contraindications: Skip after acute anterior dislocation until cleared

exercises.name: Pendulum Exercise
exercises.description: Leaning forward, let the arm swing like a pendulum to passively free the stiff shoulder.
exercises.starting_position: Stand leaning forward supporting yourself on a table with the well hand; let the sore arm hang fully relaxed.
exercises.required_movement: Let the relaxed arm swing gently forward-and-back and side-to-side in small arcs — the shoulder does no work.
contraindications: Passive only — stop if it becomes an active painful lift

exercises.name: Sleeper Stretch
exercises.description: Lying on the affected side, a gentle push rotates the shoulder internally to release tightness.
exercises.starting_position: Lie on the affected side with the sore arm underneath, elbow bent 90°.
exercises.required_movement: Use the top hand to press the forearm gently down toward the bed until the back of the shoulder stretches — hold.
contraindications: Not after recent dislocation/subluxation without clearance
Pressure must stay gentle

exercises.name: Overhead Shoulder Stretch
exercises.description: Reaching tall overhead with assistance stretches the lats and shoulder elevators.
exercises.starting_position: Standing tall; raise both arms overhead.
exercises.required_movement: Clasp the hands and reach upward and slightly back until the sides of the trunk and shoulders lengthen — hold.
contraindications: Ease off at painful overhead arcs (common in impingement)

exercises.name: Shoulder Blade Stretch
exercises.description: Gentle squeezes of the shoulder blades together to mobilise the upper back.
exercises.starting_position: Sitting or standing tall, arms relaxed.
exercises.required_movement: Draw the shoulder blades gently toward each other, hold two seconds, then relax fully — keep the shoulders low.
contraindications: Avoid hard squeezing with a rib/sternum injury

exercises.name: Wall Slides
exercises.description: Sliding the arms up a wall keeps the shoulders working symmetrically through elevation.
exercises.starting_position: Face a wall standing close; forearms vertical against it, elbows at shoulder height.
exercises.required_movement: Slide the forearms slowly up the wall as high as comfortable, then glide them back down under control.
contraindications: Stay below sharp painful arcs
Keep equal effort both sides where possible

exercises.name: Scapular Retraction
exercises.description: Repeated controlled shoulder-blade squeezes that anchor healthy shoulder mechanics.
exercises.starting_position: Sitting tall on a firm chair, arms resting loosely.
exercises.required_movement: Pull the shoulder blades together and slightly down, hold briefly without shrugging, then release completely.
contraindications: Keep the effort moderate — no breath-holding

exercises.name: Shoulder Isometric Flexion
exercises.description: Push the fist gently forward against a wall to load the shoulder without joint motion.
exercises.starting_position: Facing a wall; make a fist and place its back against the wall at waist height, elbow slightly bent.
exercises.required_movement: Press the fist gently forward into the wall at roughly 30–50% effort, hold steady, breathe, then relax.
contraindications: Early post-injury: use clinician-approved effort levels only

exercises.name: Shoulder Isometric Extension
exercises.description: Press the elbow backward against resistance to load the rear shoulder statically.
exercises.starting_position: Stand with your back near a wall; bend the elbow 90° with the upper arm alongside the body.
exercises.required_movement: Press the elbow gently backward into the wall at low-to-moderate effort, hold steady, then relax fully.
contraindications: Very low effort after acute rotator-cuff strain

exercises.name: Light Shoulder Raises
exercises.description: Raise the arms to shoulder height without weight — a safe re-entry to shoulder strength work.
exercises.starting_position: Standing tall, arms at the sides, palms facing in.
exercises.required_movement: Raise both arms forward to shoulder height only (no higher), pause, and lower slowly.
contraindications: Stop at the first painful arc — height comes later

exercises.name: Front Raises
exercises.description: Alternate controlled front raises to strengthen the front-shoulder lifting pattern.
exercises.starting_position: Standing tall; arms at the sides, palms facing the thighs (add tiny weights only when cleared).
exercises.required_movement: Raise one arm straight forward to eye height, lower it, then repeat with the other arm in a smooth rhythm.
contraindications: No added weight during active impingement pain

exercises.name: Side Raises
exercises.description: Out-to-the-side raises to shoulder height building deltoid strength safely.
exercises.starting_position: Standing tall, arms at the sides, thumbs slightly up.
exercises.required_movement: Raise both arms out to the sides to shoulder height with thumbs leading, pause, lower slowly.
contraindications: Reduce height immediately if the painful arc catches
